findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (House vote 66 to 47)
findings.note: Her recorded vote on second reading was No. The bill text (ratified version) requires county boards to process a registration only if the applicant affirmatively says they are a citizen, requires a sworn statement on citizenship if the answer is blank, and sets up removal of voters flagged as possible non-citizens from a federal database. It contains no photo ID changes.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (House vote 62 to 47)
findings.note: Her recorded vote on the House concurrence vote on the same bill was No. Bill text: https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf

She is listed as a co-sponsor (not a primary sponsor). The bill text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H1246v1.pdf) would make it a Class 2 misdemeanor for any person to demand citizenship documentation from a voter other than what State law requires at any point during the voting process. It also keeps voter photo ID images and copies of ID confidential.

HB 958, Election Law Changes (2025-2026 session). The ratified text includes a requirement that the State Board create a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database, and requires an applicant to affirmatively state US citizenship on a voter registration application. Roll call #758, Second Reading: passed 66 to 47.
